document.abstract: The TK-76 Television News Gathering Camera as described at the ll7th SMPTE Technical Conference in Los Angeles in September 1975 is shown in Figure 1. It is a small, lightweight 0 single package camera requiring only the application of a nominal 12 volt battery to generate fully encoded color signals. Shown around the cameraman's waist is a battery belt which is considered the normal source of power for the portable, man-carried, application. Since September, the product design has been completed and the camera is now in its first production cycle.

authors.bio: A. H. Lind is Manager of New Products Engineering, Studio and Control Equipment, in the Broadcast Systems Division of RCA Corporation, Camden, New Jersey. He has been a member of RCA's Broadcast Engineering staff since 1946. He has been an Engineering Manager since 1951, responsible for several Engineering Groups and/or Sections. His engineering organizations have been responsible for the development and design of many broadcast studio products-cameras, TV tape recorders, projectors, switchers, and terminal equipment. Mr. Lind received a BSEE in 1946 and an MSEE in 1949, both from the University of Wisconsin. He is a Fellow of the SMPTE, a Senior Member of the IEEE, and a member of the Franklin Institute. He is also a member of Tau Beta Pi, Eta Kappa Nu, and Pi Mu Epsilon honorary societies. He has participated in many industry technical committees. President of IEEE Group on Broadcasting, 1971–72.
